title: NASA's James Webb catches a supermassive black hole feeding
hook: JWST just captured a supermassive black hole's fuel supply in action: gas pouring into a fast-spinning disk, hinting these giants recycle their own fuel instead of just consuming and discarding it.
key_points: JWST imaged gas flowing straight into the supermassive black hole at galaxy NGC 4696's center.
A vast filament funnels material into an 800-light-year-wide spinning disk around the black hole.
Gas in that disk races around at up to 600 kilometers per second.
The black hole may recycle its own fuel: jets heat gas, which later cools and falls back in.
content_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has captured unusually detailed images of gas feeding the supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy NGC 4696. A vast filament appears to funnel material into a spinning disk 800 light-years wide, where gas races around the black hole at up to 600 kilometers per second.
extra_html: Researchers say the observation hints that black holes may recycle their own fuel rather than simply consuming and discarding it: jets from the black hole heat surrounding gas, and that gas later cools and falls back in to feed the black hole again. If confirmed, the cycle would help explain how supermassive black holes sustain themselves over cosmic time.

related.title: Black Hole Winds Starve Their Own Galaxies
related.hook: Why do the biggest galaxies hold far fewer stars than expected? New X-ray data caught a supermassive black hole blasting out winds that sweep away the gas stars need to form.

related.title: Black Holes
related.hook: A black hole is a place where gravity wins so completely that nothing — not even light — can escape once it crosses the edge called the event horizon.
